subject.title: Feature: inbound 'reply in thread' / 'rit' user directive

question: Should OpenClaw core treat suffixes like `reply in thread` or `rit` as a built-in cross-channel reply override, and which trigger vocabulary plus `replyToMode` semantics are acceptable by default?
rationale: The source-level feature absence is clear, but this would add new global natural-language parsing that can silently reroute messages and may add public config surface.

options.title: Approve a narrow core directive
options.body: Adopt only unambiguous suffixes, likely excluding bare `thread`, and require the implementation to strip all model-facing and command-facing inbound bodies while defining reply-mode override behavior.

options.title: Keep it prompt or plugin owned
options.body: Leave natural-language phrasing to agent instructions or a plugin/API seam and keep core limited to explicit reply tags plus configured reply modes.

options.title: Require explicit config first
options.body: Allow the behavior only behind a documented default-off config key with schema, docs, and upgrade-safe tests.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core directive
recommendation.body: Adopt only unambiguous suffixes, likely excluding bare `thread`, and require the implementation to strip all model-facing and command-facing inbound bodies while defining reply-mode override behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest historical signal for inbound context finalization and reply payload threading is on steipete-authored commits, so this is the best available product-routing owner.
